content:
We’re excited to announce that Iris-Lean, our port of Iris to Lean 4, is complete!
This project would not have been possible without the contributions of our open community, and we warmly thank everyone who contributed.

Iris [1] is a framework for building program logics and proving properties of programs and programming languages.
It provides a toolbox based on higher-order separation logic that can be adapted to different languages, execution models, and verification problems.
Its model is built on complete ultrametric spaces, in which it is possible to define guarded recursive types and use guarded recursion.
Developed and verified in Rocq, Iris as a framework has supported more than 160 research papers on topics including concurrent algorithms, distributed systems, low-level languages, security, probabilistic programs, and type systems.

Iris-Lean brings the same mathematical foundations and familiar Iris proof mode experience to Lean, with tactics adapted to Lean’s conventions and built using its metaprogramming facilities.
Our paper [2] describes the port, its design decisions, and new applications enabled by Lean.

For the Lean community, Iris provides reusable infrastructure for developing program logics and semantic models of type systems, together with an extensible proof mode for carrying out proofs in those logics. This makes a large body of techniques from program verification available in Lean without rebuilding the infrastructure from scratch.

For the Iris community, Lean offers access to a growing ecosystem of formalized libraries and new possibilities for proof automation and extensions through metaprogramming. The paper illustrates these benefits with a logic for continuous probabilistic programs and automation for proof search and recursive definitions. It also reports substantial speedups over Iris-Rocq in synthetic benchmarks of framing and HeapLang verification.

With the port complete, we’re excited about deeper integration into the Lean ecosystem and future work connecting Iris and Lean. Everyone is welcome to explore the project on GitHub [3], ask questions on Zulip [4], and contribute. We’d love to hear what you build with it!

Iris-Lean maintainers

[1] Iris website: https://iris-project.org/
[2] Iris-Lean paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24252
[3] GitHub repository: https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean
[4] Zulip channel: https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/490604-iris-lean
